message:
None of the three versions of the opening offer meets our 10% minimum margin. Results are for the full contract, in today's money, with 20% penalty cap, full scope, no lease engine, 3% escalation and 97% availability:
1. Fixed, $8.0M/yr, 10 years: profit -$0.31M, margin -0.5% (breaks R2).
2. Fixed, $8.0M/yr, 5 years: profit +$0.18M, margin 0.5% (breaks R2). Note the 5-year length does not break any other rule, but it is still far below 10%.
3. Hybrid, $8.0M/yr, 10 years: profit +$0.51M, margin 0.8% (breaks R2).
The main margin driver is the $8.0M fee against the fixed-price exposure over 10 years. Moving from fixed to hybrid improves margin by about 1.3 points, since the hybrid shifts part of the fee to actual running hours. The fee level is the biggest lever, so a higher fee or a lower-cost scope (for example, excluding engines or rotables) would be needed to reach 10%. I have not tested those alternatives yet; I can run them if you want.
